title: Benchmark begins public consultation on splitting out its EXW China, CIF Asia, EXW North America and EXW Europe black mass payables into black mass and black powder
gist: Benchmark proposes splitting its black mass payable indices into 'black mass' (shredded packs/cells with cathode and anode) and higher-grade 'black powder' (shredded production scrap, cathode only) after observing a ~20% payable gap, with new metal-content and impurity thresholds, an added EXW Europe LCO grade, and feedback due by 7 December 2026.

themes.theme: Black mass vs black powder grade split

insights.claim: Benchmark has observed a payable delta of approximately 20% between black mass from shredded end-of-life packs, modules, cells and jelly rolls (containing cathode and anode material) and the purer output from shredding high-grade production scrap such as cathode foil (containing only cathode material).
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A ~20% value gap means recyclers' economics depend heavily on feedstock mix (scrap vs end-of-life), which single blended indices were obscuring.
insights.quote: Benchmark has observed a notable payable delta of approximately 20% between the output derived from shredded packs, modules, cells, and jelly roll
insights.locator: Black Mass and Black Powder Distinction

insights.claim: Benchmark plans to split most of its black mass payable indices across EXW China, CIF Asia, EXW North America and EXW Europe into separate black mass and black powder categories, whereas the current methodology separates only by chemistry (NCM, LCO, LFP) and groups both intermediates together.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: New benchmark price grades will reprice recycling offtake contracts referencing Benchmark indices and improve price transparency for scrap-heavy recyclers.
insights.locator: Black Mass and Black Powder Distinction

insights.claim: The black mass versus black powder distinction is becoming increasingly prominent in the battery recycling market as a way to separate differing grades of pre-treatment output.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Market structure in recycling is maturing toward grade differentiation, similar to how primary metal markets segment by purity.
insights.quote: an increasingly prominent distinction used to distinguish the differing grades of output from the pre-treatment stage of battery recycling
insights.locator: Black Mass and Black Powder Distinction

insights.claim: Under Benchmark's proposal, NCM black mass is defined as Ni 14-25%, Co 3-8%, Mn 3-10% and Li 2-4%, whereas NCM black powder is Ni 40-55%, Co 3-15%, Mn 3-15% and Li 4.5-7%, roughly two to three times the nickel content.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Quantifies how much richer manufacturing scrap is than end-of-life feed, informing valuation of gigafactory-adjacent recyclers.

insights.claim: Benchmark proposes LCO black mass at Co 18-28% and Li 2-4% versus LCO black powder at Co 40-55% and Li 5.5-7%, and LFP black mass at Li 2-4% versus LFP black powder at Li 4-5%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: LFP feed's narrow lithium-only spread shows why LFP recycling economics are thinner than cobalt-rich LCO streams.

insights.claim: Proposed impurity limits for black powder are markedly tighter than for black mass across chemistries, for example copper and aluminium below 1% versus below 3%, carbon below 10% versus below 35%, and moisture below 2% versus below 5%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Lower impurities reduce refining costs downstream, part of why black powder commands higher payables.

insights.claim: Benchmark will not split out an EXW North America LCO black powder grade because there is little liquidity for LCO black powder in North America due to the absence of localised LCO cell production.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Highlights that North America's recycling scrap streams mirror its limited cell manufacturing footprint; black powder supply follows gigafactory location.
insights.quote: given the lack of liquidity for LCO black powder in this region due to the absence of localised LCO cell production
insights.locator: North American LCO Black Mass and EXW Europe

insights.claim: Benchmark will launch a new EXW Europe LCO black mass price grade to expand its coverage of the global black mass spot market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Signals enough European LCO black mass spot trading to warrant a dedicated price reference.
insights.locator: North American LCO Black Mass and EXW Europe

insights.claim: Benchmark is inviting feedback from active market participants on its black mass methodology changes until 7 December 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Methodology changes could take effect shortly after the consultation window, affecting index-linked recycling contracts.
